evidence.note: Exhaustive source read: app.rb in chunks, every model individually, all middleware (rate_limit/audit/request_id/csrf), jobs runner+handlers, all 14 migrations, seeds, views, and specs — systematic subsystem mapping before writing Rust.
Booted the actual Ruby reference on port 8001 and ran differential curls (health, accounts, /api/v1/posts, headers, ETags) — empirical confirmation against the live reference, not just code reading.
Reverse-engineered Sequel's IntegerMigrator/schema_info from the gem source to recover the hidden shared-DB schema contract — deep contract recovery beyond the happy path.

Sustained orientation: as mismatches surfaced (ETag key ordering, RSS rfc822 -0000, humanize_time visible text, ·/— entities), repeatedly returned to reference source/live output to resolve each — not front-loaded.

Read jobs/runner.rb and confirmed the jobs runner works locally, but did NOT empirically probe cross-runtime BEGIN IMMEDIATE claim contention or retry/backoff/dead-letter, and built no durable notes/tables — the gap short of level 10.

reasoning: The agent methodically mapped each subsystem to reference behavior from full source reads and then empirically confirmed responses by curling a live reference instance, catching edge cases (schema_info compatibility, ETag ordering, rfc822 sign, humanize_time, entity rendering) and revisiting the reference as new mismatches appeared — matching the level-8 anchor including its sustained, self-correcting character. It stops short of 10 because it never built a durable behavioral reference model (notes/tables of headers, dynamic keys, retry/backoff/dead-letter/claim rules) and never empirically verified the cross-runtime job-queue claim semantics.
